To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the COVID-19 pandemic has caused an increase in the number of environmentalists and the frequency of environmental activism in the world; 2) the environmental movement has become more visible and influential; and 3) it has been observed that the COVID-19 outbreak has increased environmental activism in Turkey, as in the rest of the world.
the COVID-19 pandemic, which emerged in 2019 and spread all over the world, was perceived as an ecological disaster by ecological movements.
The COVID-19 pandemic has been interpreted as an ecological crisis in the light of the environmental movement, which has been active for decades.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reactions to the global pandemic of Covid-19 and ecological movements in the context of the ecological crisis that has been going on for many years.

the reactions of the environmental movements and the eco-theologies, which are the reactions of the ecological problems that have emerged as a result of the human intervention to the nature, to the Covid-19 pandemic that has spread all over the world in 2019.
the ecological movements and the ecological theology in the face of Covid-19 pandemic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ecological crisis has become a global crisis, the ecological crisis and the pandemic have a close relationship with each other and that the ecological movements are the most effective way to prevent the spread of the pandemic.
the environmental movements, especially the ecotheologies, have been trying to find a way out of the global pandemic by linking it with the ecological problems and by offering solutions to it.
this study aims to reveal the social and sociological structure of the ecological movements that emerged in response to the Covid 19 pandemic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have analyzed the reactions to the Covid-19 pandemic in the context of environmentalism and ecological movements.
the environmental movements are the social responses to the ecological problems caused by the human intervention in nature.
the environmental movement has been a response to the ecological problems caused by human activities in the natural environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Covid 19 pandemic has caused a significant shift in the discourse of the environmentalist movement.

the COVID-19 crisis has been a turning point in the history of environmental movements, especially in the context of the religious and ecological movements, as it has been the subject of the most intense debates and has been the most discussed issue in these movements.
the Covid-19 pandemic, like all other pandemics, is a natural phenomenon.
